subject: Conversation stream slowdown — recovery playbook & immediate mitigations
messages:
From: Erin Zhao <erin.zhao@atlaspay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasPay Support <support@atlaspay.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Conversation stream errors — PROD (high latency)

Hi Marcus,

We started seeing elevated tail latency on the streaming/chat responses for our production webhook (region: us-east-1) around 08:40 UTC. The UI shows long pauses between chunks (~6–12s) and occasional truncated streams that never finish. This is impacting our agent-assisted flows — roughly 4% of requests fail to stream and fall back to polling which degrades experience.

Attached a snippet of a failing request (request id: atp-9c3d) and a HAR showing the timing profile. Can the Redwood team advise immediate mitigations? Our SRE is ready to coordinate.

---
Erin Zhao
Head of Integrations, AtlasPay
erin.zhao@atlaspay.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Erin Zhao <erin.zhao@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T09:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Conversation stream errors — PROD (high latency)

Thanks Erin — we see the anomaly. I'm opening an internal triage and will share immediate mitigations.

Immediate actions we can do right now:
- Flip your routing to the warmed fallback pool in us-east-1 (we can do this on your behalf for the next 2 hours) — this preserves streaming behavior while avoiding the affected edge shard.
- Temporarily enable "chunked-fallback" so if a stream stalls the client automatically receives partial outputs via polling.
- If you can, reduce max_tokens_per_chunk to 128 for the next 30–60 minutes.

I'll loop in operations to run a targeted reroute and Laura will follow with a technical root-cause and longer-lived mitigations.

Marcus
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Erin Zhao <erin.zhao@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Conversation stream errors — PROD (high latency)

Erin / Marcus — more detail from triage:

What we observed (short summary):
- Between 08:30–09:05 UTC an autoscaling config rollout inadvertently reduced the hot-KV cache reservation on a subset of us-east-1 edge servers. That resulted in more frequent KV cache evictions for large-context chat sessions.
- Eviction + higher-than-usual token pace for several multi-turn sessions caused tail latency to spike; streaming chunks were delayed while the runtime rehydrated cache and performed extra kernel memory migrations.
- Approximately 3.8% of streaming connections in that shard experienced repeated >5s chunk gaps; 0.4% terminated early and fell back to the non-streaming path.

Immediate mitigations we've applied (completed at 10:48 UTC):
1) Pinned the autoscaling config to the prior reservation for affected edge hosts.
2) Warmed an alternate edge pool and started redirecting new connections from the affected shard to that pool.
3) Deployed a runtime patch to prefer local KV hot entries for 60s after cache miss (reduces rehydration latency).
4) Pushed a recommended client setting to affected customers: reduce max_tokens_per_chunk to 128 and enable chunked-fallback.

What AtlasPay should do (recommended):
- Accept our temporary reroute for the next 2 hours (we can extend if you want). This avoids the lagging shard.
- Set chunked-fallback in your SDK (instructions attached).
- If you have a bursty period (high token rate), consider lowering concurrent_request_count or increasing keepalive to keep connections warm.

Attachments: support_dump_0630.tar.gz (server logs, request ids), mitigation_runbook_v1.pdf (step-by-step client toggles).

We'll monitor for 2 hours and then validate normal latency distribution. We'll follow up with a post-incident timeline and root-cause write-up.

Laura Bennett
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
From: Erin Zhao <erin.zhao@atlaspay.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasPay Support <support@atlaspay.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T12:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Conversation stream errors — PROD (high latency)

Laura — thanks for the quick diagnosis and for the reroute. We accepted the temporary fallback this morning at ~10:55 UTC and saw immediate improvement: chunk gaps dropped to <1s median and the rate of truncated streams is back to baseline.

A couple of follow-ups from our side:
- Can you share any guidance for client-side retries when a stream stalls mid-response? Our UI currently retries once automatically, but we may want to change the backoff behavior.
- Please confirm how long you expect the alternate pool to be used and whether this will impact throughput/cost.

Erin
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Erin Zhao <erin.zhao@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Conversation stream errors — PROD (high latency)

Erin — quick answers and next steps: 

1) Client retry guidance (short):
- If stream stalls (no chunk for >3s), attempt a single immediate reconnect with exponential backoff (initial 500ms).
- If reconnect succeeds, request remaining tokens starting from last known token id (we've added an optional resume token header for SDKs).
- If reconnect fails, use chunked-fallback to pull the latest completed partial output.

2) Alternate pool duration and impact:
- The reroute will remain in place for ~4 hours while we validate the fixed hosts and remove the pinned config rollout. We anticipate a small incremental cost (<2% unit delta) for warm pools; throughput targets should remain unchanged.

3) Postmortem / corrective action list (we will deliver a formal postmortem doc within 3 business days):
- Root cause: autoscaling config rollout reduced hot-KV reservation (mis-specified reserve flag).
- Immediate: revert reservation + warm reroute + runtime preference patch (done).
- Medium: add stronger pre-rollout load tests for cache-sensitive configs, add automated canary for KV miss rate, and add customer-facing guidance for client retry behavior.

We'll attach a short-run checklist for your SRE team and coordinate a brief call if you'd like — available 10:00–12:00 PDT tomorrow.

Thanks again for the fast sync and signals — we'll keep monitoring and I'll share the postmortem when ready.

Marcus
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
